newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Oct 24.

text.p: AT&T Corp hired John Walter, chairman of printer R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co, as its new president and chief operating officer, the Wall Street Journal reported on Thursday.
- Norfolk Southern Corp made a tender offer for Conrail Inc worth $9.1 billion.
- St. Jude Medical Inc agreed to buy Ventritex Inc for $501 million.
- Waban Inc plans to separate its BJ's chain from its HomeBase unit.
- IBM Corp formed a unit to build workstations with Intel Corp chips and Microsoft Corp software.
- Walt Disney Co is planning a $250 million campaign for the holiday season to promote its home videos like "Toy Story".
- EDS Corp posted an 8.0-percent rise in quarterly profit but foresaw slower growth during the next six months.
- Tele-Communications Inc told its equipment suppliers to suspend shipments.
- Citibank agreed to invest $2 million in a national community-development group.
- Standard & Poor's lowered the debt ratings on six Californian municipal electric companies, affecting $10 billion of debt.
- The car industry appears to be breaking out of pattern bargaining with labor unions.
- Scott Sassa, the new operating chief at Andrews Group, faces the task of boosting the company's entertainment, publishing, and toy assets.
- Charles Schwab plans to expand its mutual fund "supermarket" into bank branches and small brokerage firms.
- Wall Street analysts and investors think Signet Banking Corp should look for a company to take it over at a premium price in order to help it get back into shape.
- The Dow Jones industrial average recovered from its lows but still ended 25.34 points down at 6,036.46.
- The bond market welcomed the $12.5 billion in five-year notes issued by the U.S Treasury and helped the price of the 30-year benchmark Treasury bond to close higher.
